source_admission: Primary and institutional sources read by web retrieval on 11 October 2026, with the depth of reading recorded for each. No outside dataset or full paper is committed; working copies stay with the run records on the research drive. Earth measurements set reference values and ranges; none validates a lunar process. Values the project already cites are taken from the project register that cites them, named in 'via'.

sources.citation: Paytan & McLaughlin (2007), The oceanic phosphorus cycle, Chemical Reviews 107, 563-576
sources.use: The ocean holds about 3e15 mol of P; the residence time of dissolved P is 20-100 kyr; much of the rivers' particulate P is deposited quickly in estuaries and on shelves; about 10-30% of the total river P flux is potentially reactive and a quarter of that may be trapped in estuaries (Compton et al. 2000); P desorbing from clays as salinity rises is 2-5 times the rivers' dissolved load. The atmospheric P flux over the ocean runs from 0.08-0.4 umol m-2 day-1 over the Pacific to 0.9 over the Mediterranean, and inorganic P in mineral aerosols is bound to iron oxides or associated with Ca, Mg, Al and Fe, which are weakly soluble.
sources.access: Full text read (a teaching copy on the University of Hawaii C-MORE server), sections 3, 3.1 and 3.3.

sources.citation: Compton, Mallinson, Glenn, Filippelli, Follmi, Shields & Zanin (2000), in Marine Authigenesis: From Global to Microbial (SEPM)
sources.use: River fluxes of particulate and dissolved P and the 10-30% potentially reactive share.
sources.access: Not read; values as Paytan & McLaughlin (2007) report them.

sources.citation: Charette & Smith (2010), The volume of Earth's ocean, Oceanography 23(2)

sources.citation: Eizel-Din, Bui, Rutschmann, Failer, Grass, Kramer, Hussein & Saghayroon-Elzein (2010), Trap efficiency of reservoirs on the Nile River, River Flow 2010, Bundesanstalt fuer Wasserbau
sources.use: Siyam's (2000) form of Brune's (1953) curves, E = 100 exp(-beta I/C), with beta 0.0055, 0.0079 and 0.015 for the upper, median and lower curves of normal ponded reservoirs; Nile reservoirs trapped less than Brune's curves give.
sources.access: Full text read.

sources.citation: Brune (1953), Trap efficiency of reservoirs, Transactions of the American Geophysical Union 34(3)
sources.use: The reservoir trap-efficiency curves against capacity over inflow.
sources.access: Not read; through Eizel-Din et al. (2010).

sources.citation: Siyam (2000), Reservoir sedimentation control, PhD thesis, University of Bristol
sources.use: The exponential form of Brune's curves.
sources.access: Not read; through Eizel-Din et al. (2010).

sources.citation: Khorasani & Zhu, Phosphorus retention in lakes: a critical reassessment of hypotheses and static models, EarthArXiv preprint submitted to Journal of Hydrology
sources.use: Reviews 39 lake P-retention models on 738 observations, among them the OECD model TP_lake = k1 (TP_in / (1 + sqrt(tau_w)))^k2, refitted there with k1 = 1.729 and k2 = 0.823, and Larsen & Mercier's (1976) loss rate proportional to tau_w^-0.5. This study uses Vollenweider's simple form, k1 = k2 = 1: a lake passes on 1 / (1 + sqrt(tau_w)) of its inflowing total P.
sources.access: Full text read (preprint).

sources.citation: Vollenweider (1976), Advances in defining critical loading levels for phosphorus in lake eutrophication, Memorie dell'Istituto Italiano di Idrobiologia
sources.use: The simple mass-balance form: a lake passes on 1 / (1 + sqrt(tau_w)) of the total P it receives, tau_w its water residence in years.
sources.access: Not read; the form as Khorasani & Zhu give it.

sources.citation: Larsen & Mercier (1976), Phosphorus retention capacity of lakes, Journal of the Fisheries Research Board of Canada 33, 1742-1750
sources.use: Retention rising with water residence time.
sources.access: Not read; through Khorasani & Zhu and a search summary.

sources.citation: Xiao et al. (2017), Nutrient removal from Chinese coastal waters by large-scale seaweed aquaculture, Scientific Reports 7, 46613
sources.use: In 2014, 1,250 km2 of seaweed farms harvested 2,004,600 t dry weight and removed 9,496 t of P (7.6 t P per km2 a year); tissue P 0.34-0.52% of dry weight.
sources.access: Full text (PMC5399451) read through a fetch summary of its numbers; the figures agree with each other (9,496 t of P in 2,004,600 t of dry harvest is 0.47% P).

sources.citation: CEDA (2022), Energy efficiency considerations for dredging projects and equipment, Central Dredging Association information paper
sources.use: Trailing suction hopper dredging at Maasvlakte 2 used 0.78 kg of fuel per m3 at 10 km sailing and 1.15 kg at 27 km; a campaign table gives 0.5 L/m3 for a hopper dredger and 1 L/m3 for a backhoe. Water-injection dredging, 0.05 L/m3, moves sediment along the bed and lifts none, so it is left out of the recovery route.
sources.access: Full text read, case studies C1 and C3.

sources.use: Net calorific value of gas/diesel oil, 43.0 TJ/Gg.
sources.access: Search excerpt of the table; the chapter not read.

sources.citation: Parker, Blanchard, Gardner, Green, Hartmann, Tyedmers & Watson (2018), Fuel use and greenhouse gas emissions of world fisheries, Nature Climate Change 8, 333-337
sources.use: In 2011 fisheries landed 81 Mt at 489 L of fuel per tonne on average; small pelagic fish 42 L/t, large pelagic fish 430, demersal fish 539, crustaceans 1,739 (Table 1).
sources.access: Full text read.

sources.citation: Syers, Johnston & Curtin (2008), Efficiency of soil and fertilizer phosphorus use, FAO Fertilizer and Plant Nutrition Bulletin 18, chapter 5
sources.use: Measured by the balance method, crop recovery of applied P often ranges from 50 to 90% and can be as high as 90%; P replaced after erosion is an inefficient use of P.
sources.access: Full text of chapter 5 read.

sources.citation: Sanchez del Castillo, Cabanas Diaz, Pineda Pineda, Gonzalez Molina & Moreno Perez (2021), Evaluation of nutrient solution recirculation methods for tomato production in short cycles, Revista Mexicana de Ciencias Agricolas 12(3)
sources.use: Table 3: reusing the 20% of nutrient solution that drained applied 22.4, 26.4 and 24.8 g P per m2 against 27.2 g in the open system, 3-18% less (the text rounds the first treatment's saving to 16% for N, P and K).
sources.access: Full text read.

sources.citation: Goddek, Joyce, Wuertz, Koerner, Blaeser, Reuter & Keesman (2019), Decoupled aquaponics systems, chapter 8 in Goddek et al. (eds), Aquaponics Food Production Systems, Springer, open access
sources.use: In tilapia culture 55% of feed P ends in the sludge and 17% is excreted soluble (Neto & Ostrensky 2013); about 90% of sludge nutrients can be recovered at pH 4 (Jung & Lovitt 2011), and the worked examples mineralise 85-90% of sludge P. The 28% left for fish growth and other fates is this study's remainder.
sources.access: Full text of chapter 8 read.

sources.citation: Egle, Rechberger, Krampe & Zessner (2016), Phosphorus recovery from municipal wastewater, Science of the Total Environment 571, 522-542
sources.use: Sludge-ash routes recover 60-90% of the P the treatment works receive.
sources.access: Abstract, as resources/phosphorus_sources.json records.
